output.plan: Implement `proverb` to accept the track’s inputs plus optional keyword-only `qualifier`. Build verses by pairing each item with the next one and formatting `For want of a {current} the {next} was lost.` for every adjacent pair. If the input list is empty, return an empty string. If it has one item, return only the closing line, using the first item: `And all for the want of a {qualifier or first item}.` For longer lists, join all generated lines with `\n`, then append the closing line. Use the qualifier, when provided, only in the final line, not in the main chain. Keep the implementation data-driven so arbitrary list length and content work without hardcoded verses.
output.risks: The main risk is matching Exercism’s exact function signature and keyword-only `qualifier` handling; if the starter or tests expect a specific positional parameter name/order, the implementation must align precisely. Another risk is edge cases around one-item input, where the final line still needs to be emitted and should reflect the qualifier behavior. Finally, wording must stay exact, including punctuation and newline placement, because small formatting mismatches will fail tests.
